summary.intent: Continue working through the queued Callisto fixes one PR at a time, starting with making an unresolved changeset entry a hard error and skipping non-publishable (versionless) workspace members.
summary.outcome: Implemented both fixes: aggregation now resolves all changeset entries first and skips the whole changeset if any is unresolved, and discovery excludes versionless crates such as xtask with publish=false. Added unit and end-to-end tests, updated specs, added a changeset, ran full CI, and committed, pushed and opened a PR.

repo: Work happens in a git worktree at /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/smoke-main; PRs are opened via a body file written to /tmp and then commit/push.
Specs live in docs/specs/*.json (versioning.json, workspace.json) and must be updated alongside behavior changes; changesets go in .changeset/*.md.
Several callers consume base_versions, so versionless members are best excluded at discovery rather than handled in base_versions, following the existing precedent for versionless private npm roots.
Cargo package identity distinguishes an absent version from an inherited (workspace) version, which makes it possible to detect truly versionless crates.
Python identity reading is the risk area for the versionless filter, since it may miss version sources that current_version handles.
`just ci` is the full pipeline used to validate PRs; some tests fail in the sandbox independent of changes (three known sandbox failures).
Error code E013 is the missing-version-field error that previously aborted the whole run for versionless members.

code.finding: Changeset application loop was split into a resolve-all-entries phase followed by an apply phase, so any unresolved entry skips the entire changeset instead of partially applying it.
Discovery now drops cargo members with no version (e.g. xtask with publish=false), mirroring how versionless private npm roots are already dropped; discovery test added here.
An existing mixed-entry changeset test encoded the old partial-apply behavior and had to be rewritten.
Hosts the new end-to-end test for the unresolved-entry re-bump through the binary.

workflow: Prefer the Edit tool over heredocs when appending to test files.
After a structural edit, check for leftover redundant nested blocks and reformat; compiling does not catch them.
Run the tests to find which existing ones encode the old behavior before rewriting them.
Choose the narrowest fix location (discovery) when many callers consume a shared function.

friction: Initial edit left two redundant nested blocks that needed a cleanup pass.
Three tests fail in the sandbox for environmental reasons, which adds noise when looking for real regressions.
A heredoc attempt for adding the end-to-end test was abandoned in favor of the Edit tool.
An earlier PR body had the wrong criterion id (CLI-INIT-12 instead of CLI-INIT-10) and needed a correction.
open_items: Remaining queue: legacy removals, release-commit allow-list and registry binding, first-release preflight (taken package name currently reported as already published, E320), metadata checks, and cheap test fixes.
Release PR #349 is open from earlier merges and has not been touched.
Python identity reader may miss version sources handled by current_version, so the versionless filter should be checked for Python projects.
First-publish guidance on tokens and trusted publishing in publishing.md is hedged and needs the user's verification.
PR #350 (init defaults) is awaiting review, and the new PR for the changeset hard-error and versionless-member fix is also open.
